text: {"user":"My sister’s birthday is coming up and I want to give her a “spa day” gift. I’m thinking of booking a full package that includes a massage, facial, and a manicure, and I’d also like to add a couple of small items like scented candles and bath salts. Can you help me plan what to include and how to structure the gift so it feels thoughtful?","plus_response":"For the spa day, consider downgrading the package to just the one or two most likely-to-be-enjoyed services (e.g., massage + manicure), and skip or remove anything that could be redundant for her (like adding all three treatments). You can still make it feel complete by focusing the included services and adding a simple matching “self-care” touch—like a small set of bath salts or a single candle—rather than stacking multiple categories. If the venue offers an easy add-on, pick one small add-on you can personally curate instead of committing to the full multi-service bundle; that way the gift reads intentional, not purchased in bulk.","minus_response":"A full spa package is a great approach—if you’re already planning to include a massage, facial, and manicure, I’d keep the set intact because it creates a complete experience rather than a partial one. For the extra items, keep the candles and bath salts as a nice complement so she can extend the day at home; the combination feels luxurious and “more like a real treat” than a single item. Structure the gift by pairing each service with a matching personal note (e.g., one note for the facial, one for the manicure, one for the bath items) so the day feels cohesive and special."}
